What is photosynthesis? Mention IS 15907:2010.

### What is Photosynthesis?

**Photosynthesis** is the fundamental biological process by which green plants, algae, and photosynthetic bacteria transform light energy (primarily sunlight) into chemical energy. 

Using chlorophyll (the green pigment in plant cells), plants absorb light energy to convert carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) from the air and water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$) from the soil into glucose ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6$), releasing oxygen ($\text{O}_2$) as a vital byproduct.

$$\text{6CO}_2 + \text{6H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{Sunlight \& Chlorophyll}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6 + \text{6O}_2$$

This energy synthesis relies heavily on **Photosynthetically Active Radiation (PAR)**—the spectral waveband of solar radiation from 400 to 700 nanometers that photosynthetic organisms use to drive carbon fixation.

---

### Connection to Indian Standards: IS 15907:2010

In modern agriculture, controlling solar radiation and light intensity to optimize photosynthesis while preventing crop scorching is governed by technical standards.

* **Standard Title**: **IS 15907:2010** — *Textiles — Agrotextiles — High Density Polyethylene (HDPE) Woven Nets for Shade Application — Specification*
* **Regulatory Classification**: 
  * **[Mandatory QCO / Standard Scheme]**: Covered under the *Agro Textiles (Quality Control) Order* issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Govt. of India, requiring compulsory BIS certification (ISI Mark) for manufacture, import, or sale in India.
  * **[General Guidance]**: Defines structural, mechanical, UV-stabilization, and shading factor requirements for shade nets used in greenhouses and open-field farming.

#### Relevance to Photosynthesis:
IS 15907:2010 specifies the parameters for agrotextile shade nets (such as 25%, 35%, 50%, 75%, or 90% shade factor ratings). These nets regulate the quantum of photosynthetically active light reaching the plant canopy, maintaining optimal leaf temperature, microclimate humidity, and preventing photo-inhibition (damage to photosynthetic machinery caused by excessive sunlight).

> **Note**: Specific QCO enforcement dates, testing parameters, and standard revisions must be verified on the official BIS e-portal (`manakonline.in` / `services.bis.gov.in`) as statutory requirements are subject to ministry gazette updates.

---

### Clarification Regarding IS 15907:2010

There appears to be a misunderstanding regarding the scope of the standard you mentioned. 

**IS 15907:2010 does not apply to ceramic tableware.** 

As detailed in the official BIS database:
*   **IS 15907:2010** is titled: *"Textiles — Agrotextiles — High Density Polyethylene (HDPE) Woven Nets for Shade Application — Specification."* It is exclusively concerned with the performance and physical requirements of agricultural shade nets, not ceramics or kitchenware.

### Ceramic Tableware Standards
Ceramic tableware, including vitrified and glazed products, is governed by different standards depending on the specific product type and its intended use. The primary standard for ceramic tableware (specifically vitrified/porcelain) is:

*   **IS 15909:2010**: *Vitreous Sanitary Appliances — Vitreous China — Specification.* (Note: This is for sanitary ware).
*   **IS 2857:2018**: *Porcelain Dinnerware — Specification.* This standard covers the requirements for composition, water absorption, thermal shock resistance, and leaching of harmful substances (like lead and cadmium) in porcelain dinnerware.

### Compliance Directive
If you are looking for information on mandatory quality requirements for ceramic tableware (e.g., QCO compliance, lead/cadmium limits, or testing), please note:
1.  **[General Guidance]**: Always verify the correct Indian Standard for your specific product category on the [BIS Know Your Standards](https://www.services.bis.gov.in/php/BIS_2.0/bisconnect/knowyourstandards/indian_standards/isdetails) portal.
2.  **[Mandatory QCO]**: Please check the latest *Quality Control Orders* issued by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) or the Ministry of Commerce and Industry to see if your specific category of ceramic tableware has been brought under mandatory BIS certification.

messages.content: what is ceramic tableware

**Ceramic tableware** refers to dishes, plates, bowls, cups, mugs, and serving vessels made from clay and other non-metallic inorganic materials, which are shaped and permanently hardened by heat treatment (firing at high temperatures). 

It is widely used in households, hotels, and restaurants due to its aesthetic appeal, heat resistance, non-reactivity with food, and durability.

---

### Classification & Regulatory Status

* **Classification:** **[Mandatory QCO]** / **[General Guidance]**
* *Note on Mandatory Status:* The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, has notified Quality Control Orders (QCOs) covering ceramic tableware and kitchenware to ensure food safety and prevent heavy metal contamination (such as Lead and Cadmium leaching). Under these orders, manufacturers and importers must obtain a **BIS License (ISI Mark)** under Scheme-I of BIS Conformity Assessment Regulations before manufacturing, importing, or selling in India.

> *Verification Statement:* This product/standard requires verification on the official BIS portal ([services.bis.gov.in](https://www.services.bis.gov.in) / [manakonline.in](https://www.manakonline.in)) as standard requirements, applicable QCO dates, and revision statuses are subject to official gazette notifications.

---

### Main Types of Ceramic Tableware

1. **Earthenware:** Fired at lower temperatures (approx. 1000°C–1150°C). It is porous and usually glazed to make it waterproof and food-safe.
2. **Stoneware:** Fired at medium-to-high temperatures (approx. 1200°C–1300°C). Dense, non-porous, highly durable, and chip-resistant.
3. **Porcelain:** Fired at very high temperatures (above 1200°C–1400°C). Highly vitrified, non-porous, smooth, and translucent.
4. **Bone China:** Made from clay, feldspathic material, and bone ash. Extremely strong, lightweight, highly translucent, and durable.

---

### Relevant Indian Standards (IS) for Ceramic Tableware

| Product Category | Applicable Indian Standard | Key Technical Requirements |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Earthenware Dinnerware** | **IS 2857** | Craze resistance, thermal shock resistance, water absorption limit. |
| **Bone China Tableware** | **IS 14179** | Minimum bone ash content, translucency, glaze hardness, mechanical strength. |
| **Fine China / Porcelain Ware** | **IS 6988** | High vitrification, acid/alkali resistance, glaze durability. |
| **Lead & Cadmium Extraction Limits** | **IS 15997 / IS 16035** | Crucial health safety test measuring the permissible leaching of Lead (Pb) and Cadmium (Cd) into food. |

---

### Core Safety & Quality Tests Conducted in BIS Labs

1. **Lead and Cadmium Release Test:** Ensures heavy metals do not leach into acidic foods or hot liquids.
2. **Thermal Shock Test:** Checks if the dish can withstand sudden temperature changes without cracking.
3. **Crazing Resistance Test:** Verifies that fine cracks do not form in the glaze over time.
4. **Water Absorption Test:** Ensures the body of the ceramic does not absorb moisture, preventing microbial growth.
5. **Microwave and Dishwasher Safety:** Tests for glaze dullness, heat retention, and structural integrity.

---

### How to Verify Genuine BIS Certification for Ceramic Tableware

1. Look for the authentic **ISI Mark** printed on the product or packaging along with the **CM/L (Certificate of Manufacture / Licence Number)**.
2. Verify the CM/L number on the official **BIS Care Mobile App** using the *'Verify License'* feature to confirm manufacturer details and valid product scope.

---

### Sources & Official References

* **BIS Standards Portal:** [services.bis.gov.in](https://www.services.bis.gov.in/php/BIS_2.0/bisconnect/knowyourstandards/indian_standards/isdetails)
* **Manakonline (e-BIS Portal):** [manakonline.in](https://www.manakonline.in)
* **BIS Mandatory Certification Products List:** [bis.gov.in/product-certification/products-under-compulsory-certification/](https://www.bis.gov.in/product-certification/products-under-compulsory-certification/)
* **Official BIS Portal:** [bis.gov.in](https://www.bis.gov.in)
